manifestations of ABL include acanthocytosis. These abnormal shaped cells comprise 50% or more of circulating erythrocytes and were among the earliest laboratory features of the disorder (see Figure 1). Their structure inhibits rouleaux formation, leading to extremely low erythrocyte sedimentation rates. Anemia has been reported in some cases of ABL [28]. The likely cause was deficiencies of iron, folate, and other nutrients secondary to fat malabsorption.
